solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Saddled with the responsibility for thigh bone, badly fractured

indicators.note: a bone that is fractured is broken up, so these letters are reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A patient has to deal with a nasty broken thigh bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly fractured' reads as one phrase, but 'badly' belongs to the fodder: THIGH BONE BADLY is the pool and 'fractured' alone signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To be left holding the baby is an idiom for being stuck with a burden someone else should share.

clue.text: Round and round being bombastic

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O
rotund means round or plump

explanation.surface: Someone going round and round in circles while puffing themselves up.
explanation.definitionFit: Orotund describes a pompous, inflated style of speech, which is what bombastic language is.

clue.text: 509? That's the Deep South

parts.note: in Roman numerals D is 500 and IX is 9
i.e. (id est) means that is

explanation.surface: A number puzzle whose answer is a region of the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Dixie is the nickname for the southern states of the US, the Deep South.

clue.text: Pantless appointments fixed, like Jared Kushner's?

indicators.note: appointments that are fixed have been rigged, so the remaining letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word 'pant' is taken away from the letters of appointments

explanation.surface: A jibe that Trump's son-in-law got his White House job through family ties.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove P, A, N, T from APPOINTMENTS ('less') and 'fixed' rearranges the rest, POIMENTS, into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Kushner, married to Ivanka Trump, was given a senior advisory role by his father-in-law, a textbook case of favouring relatives.

clue.text: Give up small blanket in the dryer

parts.note: a throw is a light blanket draped over furniture
a towel is what dries you

explanation.surface: A little blanket has been put through the tumble dryer.
explanation.definitionFit: Throwing in the towel, from a boxer's corner conceding, is an idiom for surrendering.

clue.text: They say XL-size top is superior

indicators.note: what people say is heard rather than read, so the words are taken by sound

parts.note: an XL-size top is an XL, and spoken in the plural, XLs, it sounds like the answer

explanation.surface: A claim that extra-large shirts are the best ones.
explanation.definitionFit: To excel is to be better than others, outstanding.

clue.text: See 1
Two-sided bail-out subsequently covered

indicators.note: covered means the rearranged letters wrap around the other piece
out signals the letters of bail are thrown out of their order

parts.note: subsequently means later

explanation.surface: A financial bail-out, afterwards hushed up, involving two parties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bail-out' looks like a financial rescue, but the hyphen hides an anagram signal; 'covered' wraps the scrambled letters around the word for afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Bilateral means involving or having two sides, as in a bilateral agreement.

clue.text: Be lurid, rudely showing bum? One might!

definitions.text: Be lurid, rudely showing bum? One might!

indicators.note: rudely means roughly or crudely, so the letters of 'be lurid' are knocked into another order

explanation.surface: Being lewd by flashing your backside: someone on a building site might.
explanation.walkthrough: A builder's bum is the British joke about a workman whose trousers slip down as he bends over.
explanation.definitionFit: Builders are stereotypically the ones whose backsides show above sagging trousers on site.

clue.text: In essence, psychology relaxing trick

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so the central letters of each word are taken

explanation.surface: A relaxation technique, at heart, is a psychological con.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoax is a deception or practical joke played on someone.

clue.text: After a drink, copper rejected mostly silly form of defence

indicators.note: copper and the rest come after the drink, in that order

parts.note: port is a fortified wine
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the letters are read backwards
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: silly is taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: After a drink, a policeman rejects a silly way of defending oneself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims SILLY to SILL and 'rejected' reverses it to LLIS. 'copper' looks like a policeman but is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A portcullis is the heavy grille lowered to bar a castle gateway, a defensive structure.

clue.text: Bear to the audience: are you lively?

indicators.note: what an audience hears is spoken aloud, so the phrase is taken by its sound

parts.note: lively means pert, so the question is 'are you pert', which said quickly sounds like the answer

explanation.surface: Someone asks a bear, in front of onlookers, whether it feels perky.
explanation.definitionFit: Rupert Bear is a long-running British children's cartoon character in checked trousers and scarf.

clue.text: Rich water provider awaiting completion

parts.note: a well supplies water
a task still to do has not been finished

explanation.surface: A wealthy water supplier whose project isn't yet finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-to-do is an idiom for prosperous or wealthy.

clue.text: To begin with, as duke, I do own cleared right to nominate a parish priest

definitions.text: right to nominate a parish priest

indicators.note: to begin with points at the opening letters of the next two words

parts.note: 'I do' is what is said in wedding vows

indicators.note: a word cleared has its contents emptied, leaving just its outer letters

explanation.surface: A duke declares he owns the right to appoint the local vicar.
explanation.definitionFit: An advowson is an English church-law term for the patron's right to present a clergyman to a benefice.

clue.text: Composer heard frequently with another

indicators.note: heard means spoken aloud, so the word is taken by how it sounds

parts.note: frequently means often, said with a silent t
another composer, J S Bach

explanation.surface: A composer often heard alongside another one.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacques Offenbach wrote operettas including Orpheus in the Underworld with its famous can-can.

clue.text: A couple of artists in a skirt

parts.note: a couple says the artist abbreviation appears twice, so this is the first RA
RA is a Royal Academician, a distinguished artist

explanation.surface: Two painters dressed in a skirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A ra-ra is a short flounced skirt like a cheerleader's, popular in the 1980s.

clue.text: Missing a train, one father finding island

indicators.note: missing means without, so the letter is removed

parts.note: train is taken as written before the removal
one is the Roman numeral I
dad is a father

explanation.surface: A dad misses his train but ends up on a Caribbean island.
explanation.definitionFit: Trinidad is the larger island of Trinidad and Tobago in the Caribbean.

clue.text: Fraction of cheap fluff oddly discarded

indicators.note: throwing away the odd-numbered letters leaves the second, fourth and so on of each word

explanation.surface: Part of some cheap padding has been thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: A half is the fraction one over two.

clue.text: Cancel shambolic arrangement left by Mike and Charlie

indicators.note: an arrangement puts the letters in a new order
left by means abandoned by, so these letters go

parts.note: Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Scrap a chaotic set-up that two people walked out on.
explanation.walkthrough: Take M and C out of SHAMBOLIC and rearrange the remaining SHABOLI.
explanation.definitionFit: To abolish something is to do away with it formally, as one would cancel a law.

clue.text: The woman's lardy representation in traditional art

parts.note: her is the possessive for a woman

indicators.note: a representation renders the letters of lardy in another form

explanation.surface: A portrait of a plump woman in an old-fashioned style.
explanation.definitionFit: Heraldry, the design of coats of arms, is a centuries-old craft of symbolic emblems.

clue.text: Part of the church, after winter hurricane, will ultimately deteriorate

indicators.note: after says the church part comes second, following the letters picked from the storm words
ultimately means at the end, so the final letter of each word is taken

parts.note: the apse is the rounded end of a church

explanation.surface: A church damaged in a winter storm will eventually fall apart.
explanation.definitionFit: To relapse is to slip back into a worse state, as a patient's health does.

clue.text: Fast pace of cholecystectomy?

definitions.meaning: removing the gall bladder is a ..., a gall operation

explanation.surface: A medical-sounding question about how quickly surgery goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallop is the quickest gait of a horse; read as GALL OP it is a gall-bladder operation.

clue.text: Forlorn county actors

parts.note: Down is a county of Northern Ireland
the cast is the set of actors in a show

explanation.surface: A miserable provincial theatre company.
explanation.definitionFit: Downcast means dejected, low in spirits.

clue.text: Unable to disperse cloud

indicators.note: dispersing scatters, so the letters of unable are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A cloud that just won't go away.
explanation.definitionFit: A nebula is a vast cloud of interstellar gas and dust.

clue.text: Aristocrat in pub, working

parts.note: a bar is a pub
on means operating, working

explanation.surface: A nobleman doing a shift in a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A baron is a member of the lowest rank of the British peerage.

clue.text: Subject to a ban that's expired looking poorly inside

indicators.note: inside places this piece within the other

parts.note: expired means died
sallow means of a sickly yellowish complexion

explanation.surface: Something banned that died because it was unwell inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Disallowed means forbidden or not permitted, as a goal ruled out.

clue.text: Ready to appear in The Pirate Returns?

indicators.note: Returns says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the words that follow, spanning their join

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sequel film title, The Pirate Returns, about to be released.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ripe is mature and ready, as a plan ripe for launch.

clue.text: Ruler's quiet laugh returned

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: ha is a laugh

explanation.surface: A monarch gives a soft chuckle back.
explanation.definitionFit: The shah was the title of the monarch of Iran.

clue.text: Performer pranced around securing Spanish approval

indicators.note: securing means holding, so the rearranged letters hold the other piece
around signals the letters of pranced are turned about into another order

parts.note: olé is the Spanish cry of approval

explanation.surface: A dancer prancing about to Spanish cheers.
explanation.definitionFit: A pole dancer is an entertainer who dances around a vertical pole.
